style.vernacular: Low-rise concrete-block and rendered houses painted cream, ochre, salmon or sky blue, with galvanised corrugated lamina roofs (or flat concrete slabs), barred windows and walled compounds; colonial-style single-storey casas with red clay-tile roofs survive in older barrios; recent glass-and-concrete towers and malls sit on the volcano-valley slopes. Earthquake-driven construction favours thick columns and short buildings.
style.ornament: Colourful naif murals and tile mosaics in the style of Fernando Llort; Spanish colonial arched corridors and wooden doors on older churches; Neo-Gothic and eclectic church towers; exposed concrete buttresses; bahareque (wattle-and-daub) and adobe heritage at Joya de Ceren; flags and national shield on public buildings.

sources.what: valley location at about 650 m, tropical wet-and-dry climate, repeated earthquake destruction of colonial buildings, styles from neo-Gothic to modernist, local ceramic tile and concrete block industry
colourful facade, history of repeated rebuilding, 1990s concrete cathedral
wattle-and-daub walls and adobe columns of the Maya village buried by ash
